programme.desc: Monty begins his journey in a prairie, the original American flowering wilderness. Much of the prairie has disappeared, but he meets a couple who have revived the tradition and enjoy showing it to him in full bloom.

programme.title: Monty Don's American Gardens
programme.desc: Monty goes South to explore gardens of early independent America and learns how the history of this part of the country is still very much evident in the places and people he meets. He visits the famous garden of President Thomas Jefferson.

programme.title: Monty Don's American Gardens
programme.desc: Monty explores the scenery of the west coast of America. He begins his journey in Arizona where he learns about cacti and marvels at the sight of them in the desert and in private gardens where they have replaced traditional plants and lawns.

programme.title: Monty Don's British Gardens
programme.desc: Monty Don travels from the north-west coast of Scotland to the north-east coast of England, from historic reconstructions to modern re-inventions. He visits some of the most inhospitable places in the country and finds gardens that are flourishing.

programme.title: Monty Don's British Gardens
programme.desc: Monty travels across some of the country's landscapes, heading across the north of England to Northern Ireland. Here, Monty sees the ingenuity, passion and determination of British people to garden and create gardens, no matter what the canvas.

programme.title: Monty Don's British Gardens
programme.desc: Monty travels across the middle of the country, from Wales to Norfolk. He comes across gardens for gnomes, much-loved, well-tended allotments and extravagant gardens that bankrupted their owners.

programme.title: Monty Don's British Gardens
programme.desc: Monty travels across the middle of the country, from Wales to Norfolk. He comes across gardens for gnomes, much-loved, well-tended allotments and extravagant gardens that bankrupted their owners.

programme.title: Monty Don's British Gardens
programme.desc: Monty Don explores the most densely populated part of the country, London and the home counties. He visits some of London's gardens, including a special one on a barge, as well as a beautifully restored garden close to where he grew up in Hampshire.

programme.title: Monty Don's British Gardens
programme.desc: Monty travels across the south-west of the country to visit some of Britain's most exotic gardens. On this journey, Monty also goes to some of the country's most historic gardens, as well as some challenging contemporary ones.

programme.title: Monty Don's Japanese Gardens
programme.desc: Monty continues his travels to learn about the art of Japanese stonemasonry and the famous tea ceremonies and their accompanying gardens, before finally taking a lesson in the delicate art of traditional flower arranging.

programme.title: Monty Don's Japanese Gardens
programme.desc: Monty Don returns to Japan during the fiery blaze of autumn. He visits the three great gardens of Japan to learn how they protect the garden from the coming winter and learns how the Japanese are weaving nature into their concrete urban jungle.

programme.title: Monty Don's Paradise Gardens
programme.desc: In Morocco, Monty discovers the wide variety of paradise gardens. He begins just outside the city of Marrakesh in an enormous royal walled meadow, The Agdal. From there he moves to the heart of the town where he comes upon a tiny garden.

programme.title: Monty Don's Paradise Gardens

programme.title: Monty Don's Paradise Gardens
programme.desc: In Turkey Monty is dazzled by a display of the Ottoman Empire's favourite flower, the tulip, and learns of its sacred significance. Travelling further East to India he encounters a new type of spirituality in the tomb gardens of the Mughal Empire.

programme.title: Monty Don's Italian Gardens

programme.title: Monty Don's Italian Gardens

programme.title: Monty Don's Italian Gardens

programme.title: Monty Don's Italian Gardens

programme.title: The Rise of Rome
programme.desc: Addressing the simple question of how Rome became so powerful; considering the role of the city's geography and the republic's unique political structure, both of which allowed Rome to flourish.

programme.title: The Rise of Rome
programme.desc: The beginning of the rise of Rome; unpacking some key myths, including the epic of Aeneas and the story of Romulus and Remus, to gain insight into the city's founding; reflecting on neighboring civilizations such as the Etruscans.

programme.title: The Rise of Rome
programme.desc: Tales and literature from early Rome that share great insight into Roman values and what the Romans identified as the qualities of ideal citizens; how a few Roman heroes embody ideals of courage, resourcefulness, determination and more.

programme.title: The Rise of Rome
programme.sub-title: The Early Republic and Rural Life
programme.desc: The transition from the monarchy to the republic, a new era of government that would carry the city through half a millennium; wading through mythology, propaganda and Roman historical sources to reconstruct how the transition happened.

programme.title: Great Ancient Civilizations of Asia Minor
programme.desc: The lands around the central Turkish plateau historically "face" two ways; the western and southern shores are drawn to Greece and Europe; the mountain-ringed interior is linked to Iran and Asia proper.

programme.title: Great Ancient Civilizations of Asia Minor
programme.desc: Neolithic Anatolians are among the first farmers and herders, dwelling in villages with sophisticated technology and organization; they learn to write and build palaces and cities from the Sumerians to the south.

programme.title: Great Ancient Civilizations of Asia Minor
programme.desc: Beginning as invaders from the Balkans, the Indo-European people called the Hittites overrun Anatolia's core with their war chariots; they create a dynasty that rivals the Egypt of Ramses II.

programme.title: Great Ancient Civilizations of Asia Minor
programme.desc: Hittite kings become the first of many conquerors who leave their mark on the land; near their ritual capital of Hattusas, they carve from rock an open-air shrine to their thousands of gods; shortly thereafter, Hattusas is sacked and abandoned.

programme.title: Great Pharaohs of Ancient Egypt

programme.title: Great Pharaohs of Ancient Egypt

programme.title: Great Pharaohs of Ancient Egypt

programme.title: The Remarkable Science of Ancient Astronomy
programme.desc: Whether the popular view of Stonehenge as a sophisticated astronomical calculator presided over by Druids is correct; addressing the evidence; surveying the archaeological record to discover the most probable function of Stonehenge.

programme.title: Cities of the Ancient World
programme.desc: Cities are integral to modern lives; why wandering ancient humans leave the forests and plains to create settlements; the fundamental question of "why" is the first step toward understanding the inhabitants and lessons from ancient cities.

programme.title: Cities of the Ancient World
programme.sub-title: Çatalhöyük - First Experiment in Urban Living
programme.desc: Imagining a city with no streets, public buildings or common spaces; the world's first city offers an intriguing window into life in the Neolithic era; exploring the remains of Çatalhöyük's family housing, murals and religious shrines.

programme.title: Cities of the Ancient World
programme.desc: The story of the walls of Jericho in the Book of Joshua; looking past the biblical story; what architectural remains suggest about Jericho, whose ritual spaces help create a community and whose walls help define the urban environment.

programme.title: Cities of the Ancient World
programme.desc: Looking at one of the most marvelous cities in the ancient world; Uruk exhibits many of the hallmarks of ancient civilization; division of labor among its craftsmen; a class hierarchy that includes professional priests; records of art and literature.

programme.title: Ancient Mesopotamia: Life in the Cradle of Civilization
programme.desc: Egypt, Greece and Rome may be better known to the public; more written evidence survives from Mesopotamia; embarking on a journey through over 3,000 years of history; learning why Mesopotamia's rediscovery is so valuable.

programme.title: Ancient Mesopotamia: Life in the Cradle of Civilization
programme.desc: The enormous value of plant and animal domestication; the theories about the transition from a hunter-gatherer lifestyle to agriculture; the challenges that farming presents; a perspective on the cultural sophistication of pre-agrarian peoples.

programme.title: Ancient Mesopotamia: Life in the Cradle of Civilization
programme.desc: Travel is dangerous but people transport valuable goods, perhaps via chains of merchants; daily life in Neolithic Mesopotamia, where homes and villages reflect a simple society; evidence of intricate pottery shows that people care about aesthetics.

programme.title: Ancient Mesopotamia: Life in the Cradle of Civilization
programme.sub-title: Eridu and Other Towns in the Ubaid Period
